skill.name: dependency-audit-assistant
skill.description: Audits project dependencies for known vulnerabilities, outdated packages, dependency tree risk, and license compliance concerns.
skill.summary: Guides dependency security, freshness, and license compliance audits across common package ecosystems.
skill.author: CrazyDubya

security_audit.summary: Most high-severity static hits are false positives from markdown examples and reference material. Real concerns remain in the Bash helper: it uses a fixed temporary file and can install unpinned tools from public registries. No prompt-injection text or data-exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: The license helper installs missing audit tools automatically.
remediation.suggestion: Replace automatic installs with clear instructions, pinned versions, and explicit user confirmation before any package installation.

remediation.issue: The script writes dependency license output to a fixed /tmp/licenses.json path.
remediation.suggestion: Use mktemp for a unique file, set restrictive permissions, and clean it with a trap on exit.

remediation.issue: The skill recommends state-changing package manager commands in command references.
remediation.suggestion: State that fix commands require user approval and should run only after review and tests.

content.value_statement: Dependency risks hide in package trees, outdated versions, and unclear licenses. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through focused audits and prioritized remediation.
actual_capabilities: Detects common package manager files for JavaScript, Python, Ruby, Java, Go, Rust, and PHP projects.
Guides package audit commands and summarizes vulnerabilities by severity, package, version, and available fix.
Checks outdated dependencies and separates patch, minor, and major upgrade work.
Reviews dependency licenses and flags GPL, AGPL, unknown, or custom license concerns.
Analyzes direct and transitive dependency risk, including abandoned packages and duplicate versions.
Produces prioritized remediation plans for releases, security reviews, and maintenance work.
limitations: Results depend on installed package manager tools and current advisory databases.
The skill cannot prove exploitability without application source, runtime exposure, and usage context.
License guidance supports triage and is not legal advice.
Some audit commands may require network access and explicit user approval.

use_cases.title: Pre-release security review
use_cases.description: Audit dependencies before deployment and identify fixes that should block release.

use_cases.title: License compliance triage
use_cases.description: Find GPL, AGPL, unknown, or custom licenses before shipping a commercial product.

use_cases.title: Open source maintenance planning
use_cases.description: Group outdated packages by upgrade risk and create a practical update plan.

prompt_templates.title: Run a basic dependency audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this repository for dependency vulnerabilities. Detect the package manager, run safe audit checks, and summarize fixes by severity.

prompt_templates.title: Review licenses for release
prompt_templates.prompt: Check dependency licenses for this project. Flag GPL, AGPL, unknown, and custom licenses, then suggest next review steps.

prompt_templates.title: Plan dependency updates
prompt_templates.prompt: Find outdated dependencies and group updates as patch, minor, or major. Prioritize security fixes and low-risk upgrades first.

prompt_templates.title: Build a full remediation plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit vulnerabilities, outdated packages, licenses, and transitive dependency risk. Create a prioritized remediation plan with testing guidance.

output_examples.input: Audit an npm service before release.
output_examples.output: The report identifies one high vulnerability, seven outdated packages, and one unknown license. It recommends fixing the high vulnerability first.

output_examples.input: Review licenses for a commercial Python application.
output_examples.output: The review separates permissive, weak copyleft, strong copyleft, and unknown licenses. It highlights packages needing legal or replacement review.

output_examples.input: Create an update plan for a mixed Go and JavaScript repository.
output_examples.output: The plan groups quick patch updates, test-required minor updates, and major upgrades that need migration notes.

best_practices: Run audits before releases and after adding new dependencies.
Commit lock files and review changes before accepting automated upgrades.
Test security fixes the same way as normal dependency updates.
anti_patterns: Treating every audit warning as equally urgent.
Running forced upgrades without reading migration notes.
Ignoring transitive dependencies because they are not listed directly.

faq.question: Does this skill fix vulnerabilities automatically?
faq.answer: It recommends fixes and may suggest commands, but users should approve state-changing actions.

faq.question: Which ecosystems does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers common JavaScript, Python, Ruby, Java, Go, Rust, and PHP package workflows.

faq.question: Can it replace a security scanner?
faq.answer: No. It helps interpret scanner output and organize remediation decisions.

faq.question: Can it decide legal license questions?
faq.answer: No. It flags license risk for review, but legal counsel should decide obligations.

faq.question: Does it need internet access?
faq.answer: Some package audit and advisory checks may need network access to return current results.

faq.question: Can it audit transitive dependencies?
faq.answer: Yes. It guides dependency tree review and separates direct from transitive risk.
